feed.title: NPR Programs: Morning Edition
feed.subtitle: Morning Edition takes listeners around the country and the world with multi-faceted stories and commentaries every weekday. Hosts Steve Inskeep, Leila Fadel, Michel Martin and A Martínez bring you the latest breaking news and features to prepare you for the day.

entry.title: Trump and China's Xi discuss AI, trade and Iran war during state visit
entry.summary: U.S. President Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping met for the second time this year to much fanfare but little in the way of grand bargains.

entry.title: Former U.S. ambassador to China on Xi Jinping's visit to Washington
entry.summary: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with former U.S. Ambassador to China Nicholas Burns about Chinese President Xi Jinping's visit to Washington and what has been accomplished.

entry.title: Mortgage rates are over 7%. What it means for would-be homebuyers
entry.summary: The average mortgage rate is above 7% for the first time since January 2025. Compared with earlier this year, that interest rate means would-be homebuyers would pay hundreds more each month.

entry.title: Netanyahu rages against critics, including Mamdani, at the U.N. General Assembly
entry.summary: Middle East crises draw major focus as the U.N. General Assembly hears from Israel, the Palestinian Authority and Yemen.

entry.title: As election enters its final stretch, some Republicans are distancing from Trump
entry.summary: With less than six weeks until Election Day, a growing number of Republicans are breaking from Trump on key issues. It comes as the party is scrambling to hold onto a slim majority in Congress.

entry.title: Morning news brief
entry.summary: Takeaways from the summit between President Trump and China's Xi, three media outlets banned from the White House returned Thursday after a judge's ruling, Israel's prime minister addresses the U.N.

entry.title: 'Primetime' tells a fictionalized version of the rise of 'To Catch a Predator'
entry.summary: The rise of NBC's "To Catch a Predator" is fictionalized in the film "Primetime," starring Robert Pattinson as Chris Hansen. NPR's A Martinez speaks with director Lance Oppenheim.

entry.title: Iran's president says his country has 'no trust' in U.S. in meeting with journalists
entry.summary: NPR's Steve Inskeep was part of a small group of journalists who met with an Iranian official on the sidelines of the U.N. General Assembly in New York. He tells Leila Fadel what he learned.

entry.title: Largest international livestock crossing reopens after screwworm outbreak
entry.summary: The largest international livestock crossing on the Texas/New Mexico border opens after being shut down for more than a year because of the flesh-eating New World Screwworm fly.

entry.title: The U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve is running low. Can Venezuelan oil help?
entry.summary: Whether it's oil from Venezuela or somewhere else, the U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve needs to be refilled. The SPR is widely considered critical for energy security. We run through the challenges to refilling the reserves.
